title: Indonesia: Papuan militants kill 17
text: HRW describes the December 2018 Nduga worksite killings, disputed accounts of the victims, security operations and a lack of independent access.

title: Pengungsi Beoga Puncak minta dievakuasi
text: ANTARA interviewed a health worker seeking evacuation after two teachers were killed on 8 and 9 April 2021. Shops were closed and food was running short.

title: The Intan Jaya conflict
text: The Humanitarian Team documented violence around Sugapa and the killing of Pastor Yeremia Zanambani on 19 September 2020, alongside concerns over civilian protection.

title: Papua Monitor: second quarter 2026
text: HRM reports military operations and armed violence in Puncak and Intan Jaya during April–June 2026; security operations also in Nduga. It attributes disruption of health and education services and displacement to recurring violence and fear. It records intimidation and dispersal of Pesta Babi screenings; the documentary was released online on 22 May 2026. This is an attributed monitoring record, not independent verification of every allegation.

title: Mahkamah Agung tolak kasasi suku Awyu
publisher: WALHI / Save Papuan Customary Forests Coalition
text: The coalition reports decision 458 K/TUN/LH/2024, decided 18 September 2024, rejecting Hendrikus Woro’s cassation over PT Indo Asiana Lestari’s environmental approval. One judge dissented. PT Kartika Cipta Pratama and PT Megakarya Jaya Raya cases were separate.

title: Elegi Selatan Papua
text: Pusaka announced the 13 August 2026 Jayapura launch and discussion of a Human Rights Impact Assessment of South Papua food and energy projects. Pusaka describes impacts on customary land, communities and the environment; the event page is a description of its findings, not the full assessment.

title: A sweetness like unto death: voices of the indigenous Malind of Merauke
text: Field study documents Malind community experiences of MIFEE, land negotiation, forest conversion and changes to food systems.

title: Merauke National Strategic Project timeline
text: Pusaka timeline distinguishes the 2023 strategic-project designation and the April 2024 sugar and bioethanol task force from the rice programme. Planned area is not cleared area.

title: Four mining permits revoked in Raja Ampat
publisher: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources · 2025
text: ESDM announced revocation of ASP, MRP, KSM and Nurham mining permits. PT Gag Nikel’s permit remained; revocation does not establish ecological rehabilitation.

title: History of PT Freeport Indonesia
text: PTFI history records the first contract in 1967 and majority Indonesian ownership in 2018. Corporate history is first-party evidence, not an independent environmental assessment.

title: If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?
text: HRW documents racist abuse against Papuan students, August 2019 protests, arrests and subsequent discrimination.

title: Court ruling on internet blackout
text: Amnesty reports the Jakarta administrative court ruling that 2019 government internet throttling and shutdown were unlawful.

title: PTUN orders disclosure of Raja Ampat permit-revocation records
text: Greenpeace reports that PTUN Jakarta rejected BKPM’s objection on 14 September 2026, affirming the Central Information Commission’s 10 June 2026 decision that the four permit-revocation documents and implementation details were public information. This is a disclosure ruling, not proof of ecological rehabilitation or confirmation that the documents had been released.

title: HUT ke-59 Freeport: Bangkit Bersama Menuju Operasi Berkelanjutan
text: PTFI’s 9 April 2026 account commemorates seven employees killed in the 8 September 2025 Grasberg Block Cave wet-material incident and two killed in separate shootings in February and March 2026. It reports production at 40–50% during recovery and a target to approach full production by year-end. These are corporate statements; the target is not an achieved outcome.
